row.evidence: Partnerize's pricing page offers only quoted pricing ("Partnerize offers both a license model and a performance-based structure"), its public Brands API reference has no SCIM or user-administration endpoints, and its only IdP catalogue listing (Okta OIN) is SAML sign-in.
row.notes: New row. Quote-only: pricing is a custom license fee or a percentage-of-performance fee, quoted after a form; the page says pricing is all inclusive. No SCIM is documented on partnerize.com or in the public Brands API reference (api-docs.partnerize.com/brand), but the help centre (help.partnerize.com) is IP-restricted by Cloudflare and could not be searched, so status stays unknown rather than none. The Okta OIN app (last updated Jan 2021) ticks SAML only. The Brands API (Basic auth with User Application Key + User API key) can update the calling user's email and create network partner users, but documents no endpoints to list, invite, change or remove brand console users, so user_api_available is false by absence.

plans.name: Platform (license or performance-based)
plans.price_text: Custom quote: fixed license fee or percentage-based fee
plans.notes: No named tiers; pricing varies by service level (full program management, in-house, agency supported) and program structure.

scim.notes: No SCIM endpoint found on partnerize.com (sitemaps, llms.txt, pricing) or in the Brands API OpenAPI spec (175 paths, none SCIM). The help centre could not be loaded, so availability is null.

auth.notes: Basic auth with the Base64 of User Application Key and User API key from Account settings.

rate_limits.text: Usage-based rate limiting; 429 Too Many Requests when exceeded.

user_api.notes: The Brands API is a REST API for partnership data (campaigns, conversions, partners, invoices). User-related operations are PATCH /v3/brand/user (update the current user's email) and POST /user (create a network partner with a Partnerize login); neither manages brand team members, so 'available' is false by absence.

okta.notes: OIN page markup ticks SAML only; no provisioning features checked.

fallbacks.notes: The API reference is public; the help centre is IP-restricted (see c9), so SSO/provisioning help articles could not be read.
